;Armed conflicts and attacks
*[[War in Afghanistan (2001–present)|War in Afghanistan]], [[Afghan peace process]]
**In [[Zabul Province]], the [[Taliban]] releases two [[Foreign hostages in Afghanistan|foreign hostages]], [[Americans|American]] [[professor]] Kevin King and [[Australians|Australian]] professor Timothy Weeks, who had been held captive since being [[kidnap]]ped outside the [[American University of Afghanistan]] in 2016. Three high-ranking Taliban militants are released in exchange for the hostages. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/world-asia-50471186 (BBC News)]
**[[Afghanistan|Afghan]] [[President of Afghanistan|President]] [[Ashraf Ghani]] claims victory over [[Islamic State of Iraq and the Levant|ISIL]], citing the surrender of over 600 of their fighters in the past weeks as an example that the group has given up. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-afghanistan-islamicstate/afghanistans-president-claims-victory-over-islamic-state-idUSKBN1XT1UQ (Reuters)]
*[[Second Libyan Civil War]]
**[[Libyan National Army]] (LNA) warplanes carry out [[airstrike]]s on the port city of [[Misrata]]. The LNA say they were targeting munitions and armored vehicles that had been delivered from [[Turkey]]. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-libya-security/east-libyan-forces-target-munitions-in-misrata-with-air-strikes-idUSKBN1XT16D (Reuters)]
*[[2019–2020 Iranian protests]]
**[[Riot|Rioters]] armed with knives kill three members of [[Iran]]'s [[Armed Forces of the Islamic Republic of Iran|security forces]], bringing the death toll up to 11. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2019/11/urges-iran-restraint-reports-rioters-kill-3-soldiers-191119073050682.html (Al Jazeera)]
**[[Amnesty International]] reports that 106 protesters have been killed during the protest. Some reports indicate a much higher death toll. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-middle-east-50474405 (BBC News)] [https://nationalpost.com/pmn/news-pmn/politics-news-pmn/at-least-106-protestors-killed-in-iran-during-unrest-amnesty-international (''National Post'')]
*[[2019 Hong Kong protests]]
**After the attack on [[pro-democracy]] activist [[Jimmy Sham]] the month prior, another pro-democracy activist, [[Albert Ho]], is attacked by masked men at a minibus stop. [https://www.scmp.com/news/hong-kong/politics/article/3038480/police-investigate-alleged-attack-hong-kong-pro-democracy (''South China Morning Post'')]
*[[2019 Bolivian protests]]
**At least three people are killed and 22 injured after [[Bolivian National Police|Bolivian police]] and [[Armed Forces of Bolivia|military forces]] use armored vehicles and helicopters to unblock access to a major fuel plant that had been blockaded by supporters of former president [[Evo Morales]]. [https://www.theguardian.com/world/2019/nov/19/bolivia-clashes-police-army-break-fuel-blockade (''The Guardian'')]
**Bolivia's congress, controlled by lawmakers from Morales' [[Movement for Socialism (Bolivia)|Movement for Socialism]] (MAS) party, said it would cancel a contentious vote in the legislature that had been expected to reject Morales' resignation. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-bolivia-election/bolivian-lawmakers-seeking-to-calm-tensions-cancel-vote-on-morales-idUSKBN1XT228 (Reuters)]

;Business and economy
*[[2019 Japan–South Korea trade dispute]]
**Officials from [[Japan]] and [[South Korea]] hold their second round of trade talks as part of the [[World Trade Organization]]'s dispute settlement process. [https://www3.nhk.or.jp/nhkworld/en/news/20191119_10/amp.html (NHK World-Japan)]
**Japan and South Korea have failed to narrow their differences over Japan's export controls in the second round of bilateral talks. [https://www3.nhk.or.jp/nhkworld/en/news/20191120_07/ (NHK World-Japan)]
*Amid continuing fallout over rape allegations against [[Prince Andrew, Duke of York]], and controversy over his close friendship with convicted sex offender [[Jeffrey Epstein]], several businesses—including British banking group [[Standard Chartered]], [[KPMG]], [[Aon (company)|Aon]] and drug giant [[AstraZeneca]]—cut ties with the Prince. Pitch@Palace, an initiative founded by Prince Andrew to support entrepreneurs, removes its entire web page listing its supporters. [https://uk.sports.yahoo.com/news/prince-andrew-jeffrey-epstein-pitchpalace-kpmg-aon-095904255.html (Yahoo! News)] [https://edition.cnn.com/2019/11/18/business/prince-andrew-pitch-at-palace/index.html (CNN)]

;Health and environment
*Fifteen children are confirmed (and three more suspected) dead from [[measles]] in [[Samoa]] as the illness epidemic continues within the country. [https://www.rnz.co.nz/international/pacific-news/403586/samoa-measles-outbreak-claims-lives-of-15-children-report (Radio New Zealand)]

;International Relations
*[[Hong Kong–United States relations]], [[China–United States relations]], [[2019 Hong Kong protests]]
** The [[United States Senate|U.S. Senate]] unanimously passes the [[Hong Kong Human Rights and Democracy Act]], which mandates that the [[United States Department of State|State Department]] at least annually checks to see if [[Hong Kong]] retains enough autonomy to retain its special trade status with the [[United States]]. The Senate also unanimously passes another bill banning the sale of certain crowd-control munitions to the [[Hong Kong Police Force|Hong Kong police]]. The former's passage is condemned by [[China]]. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-hongkong-protests-usa/u-s-senate-passes-hk-rights-bill-backing-protesters-angers-beijing-idUSKBN1XT2VR?il=0 (Reuters)]
*[[Iran–United States relations]]
**The aircraft carrier [[USS Abraham Lincoln (CVN-72)|USS ''Abraham Lincoln'']] transits through the [[Strait of Hormuz]] amidst ongoing tensions between the [[United States]] and Iran. [https://www.navytimes.com/news/your-navy/2019/11/20/carrier-abraham-lincoln-transits-strait-of-hormuz-for-the-first-time-since-deployment/ (''Navy Times'')] [https://www.reuters.com/article/world/us-aircraft-carrier-strike-group-sails-through-strait-of-hormuz-idUSKBN1XT2EF/ (Reuters)]

;Law and crime
*''[[Assange v Swedish Prosecution Authority]]''
**A [[Sweden|Swedish]] prosecutor says she will drop charges of [[rape]] against [[Julian Assange]] after a review of the evidence. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-britain-assange-sweden/sweden-says-it-is-dropping-assange-rape-investigation-idUSKBN1XT1QO (Reuters)]
*[[Death of Jeffrey Epstein]]
**Two prison guards who worked at the [[Metropolitan Correctional Center, New York|Metropolitan Correctional Center]] in [[New York City]] are arrested in connection with the death of American financier and convicted sex offender [[Jeffrey Epstein]]. The guards are accused of falsifying the records of their watch the night Epstein was found dead. [https://www.washingtonexaminer.com/news/two-prison-employees-arrested-in-connection-to-epsteins-death (''Washington Examiner'')] [https://nypost.com/2019/11/19/two-jail-guards-arrested-over-jeffrey-epstein-suicide/ (''New York Post'')]
*The [[Northern Mariana Islands House of Representatives]] calls for the impeachment of [[Governor of Northern Mariana Islands|Governor]] [[Ralph Torres]] amid an ongoing [[Federal Bureau of Investigation]] investigation into his businesses. [https://www.rnz.co.nz/international/pacific-news/403640/call-for-impeachment-of-cnmi-governor (Radio New Zealand)]
*[[Crime in Germany]]
**Son of former German president [[Richard von Weizsäcker]], a physician, is stabbed to death during a lecture. The attacker is reported as 57 years old. [https://www.dw.com/en/son-of-former-german-president-stabbed-to-death-in-berlin-hospital/a-51325419 (Deutsche Welle)] [https://berlinspectator.com/2019/11/20/berlin-prominent-physician-murdered-during-lecture/ (The Berlin Spectator)]
*[[Operation Car Wash]]
**A [[Rio de Janeiro]] judge issues an arrest warrant against former [[President of Paraguay]] [[Horacio Cartes]], accusing him of operating a [[money laundering]] scheme with a friend, Dario Messer, who is prosecuted as part of Operation Car Wash. [https://www.efe.com/efe/america/politica/la-lava-jato-golpea-a-paraguay-con-pedido-de-prision-del-expresidente-cartes/20000035-4114531 (EFE)] [https://www.clarin.com/mundo/juez-brasil-ordeno-detencion-ex-presidente-paraguay-horacio-cartes-corrupcion_0_QzVTXSgu.html (''Clarín'')]
;Politics and elections
*[[Shinzō Abe]] becomes the longest-serving [[Prime Minister of Japan]]. [https://www.straitstimes.com/asia/east-asia/japans-shinzo-abe-ties-record-for-longest-serving-pm-even-as-allegations-of-misdeeds (''The Straits Times'')]
*[[2019 Chilean protests]]
**An impeachment inquiry is launched against [[Chile]]an President [[Sebastián Piñera]] due to his alleged role in the violation of human rights in the [[2019 Chilean protests|ongoing protests]]. [https://www.wsws.org/en/articles/2019/11/19/chil-n19.html (World Socialist Web Site)]
*[[Sabah Al-Khalid Al-Sabah]] is named by the [[Emir of Kuwait|Emir]] as the new [[Prime Minister of Kuwait]], replacing [[Jaber Al-Mubarak Al-Hamad Al-Sabah]]. [https://gulfnews.com/world/gulf/kuwait/kuwait-emir-appoints-foreign-minister-as-new-pm-1.67932916 (''Gulf News'')]
*[[2019 Montserratian general election]]
**After his victory in the general election, [[Easton Taylor-Farrell]] is sworn in as [[Premier of Montserrat]]. [http://rjrnewsonline.com/local/new-monsterrat-premier-easton-taylor-farrell-sworn-in (RJR News)]
*[[Silveria Jacobs]] is appointed as the new [[Prime Minister of Sint Maarten]]. [https://www.thedailyherald.sx/islands/92592-st-maarten-has-new-government (The Daily Herald)]
